answer: Real jade is valued because a gem cutter can test it in seconds and no counterfeit passes twice. An atlas of trust works the same way: every agent's route is drawn in public, and a sybil's paths all dead-end at the same empty address. Behind it sits a vault that only opens when neighbours with real stakes vouch for the keyholder. Jade can be tested, an atlas can be audited, a vault needs witnesses - cheap copies fail all three.
